_comment: EXAMPLE — stage 1 output. One file per use case under <output>/use-cases/, named <use case id>.json. The filename IS the id; stage 3 rejects a file whose `id` field disagrees with its stem. This whole output/_example/ tree is a worked example of one target's output — copy its shape, or point the pipeline at it directly with --output output/_example to smoke-test a stage.
name: Registered customer signs in with email and password
description: A customer submits credentials to the login endpoint. The application verifies them against the user store and issues a signed token that authorizes every subsequent request.

_fields.id: REQUIRED. Stable across runs — it becomes part of every threat id, so changing it breaks run-to-run diffing. Convention: UC-SCREAMING-KEBAB. Must be filesystem-safe: no slashes or spaces.
_fields.name: Recommended. One line, appears verbatim in the stage 3 prompt.
_fields.description: Recommended. Two or three sentences on what actually happens. The agent's orientation before it reads any code.
_fields.entry_points: Optional. Routes or handlers. Useful to stage 2, ignored by stage 3.
_fields.source_refs: Optional. Files stage 1 found relevant. Stage 2 turns these into '%% file:' hints in the diagram.
_fields._any_other_key: Ignored by stage 3, so stages 1 and 2 can carry extra fields without coordinating.
